reason: The text demonstrates the opposite. The Hebrew midwives (Shiphrah and Puah) actively express their views when confronted by Pharaoh. When he questions them about why they preserved the Hebrew children rather than killing them (וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶן מַדּוּעַ עֲשִׂיתֶן הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה), they respond directly with an explanation (וַתֹּאמַרְןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה). They openly justify their actions, demonstrating that they are not discouraged from expressing their views. Rather, they fear God (וַתִּירֶאן אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים) more than the Pharaoh's orders, and they voice this implicitly through their disobedience and explicit explanation.
